title: Approve vaginal pH modulation for on-demand non-hormonal contraception

concept.text: Enable woman-controlled pregnancy prevention through a non-hormonal vaginal pH-modulating product used around intercourse. Phexxi achieved approval, but its efficacy is substantially below long-acting contraception. Proposed completion test: FDA approval specifically for on-demand pregnancy prevention, based on a phase 3 study measuring cumulative pregnancy incidence over seven menstrual cycles and reviewing local and urinary safety. Test set by: FDA; its review accepted a seven-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate of 13.7% with a 95% confidence interval of 10.0–17.5%. This was not a Pearl Index below 2. Reported achieved: FDA approved Phexxi on 22 May 2020. Sources given: [FDA Phexxi approval letter](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/208352Orig1s000ltr.pdf) ; [FDA multidisciplinary efficacy and safety review](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/208352Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf).

page.title: On-demand contraception by vaginal pH modulation
page.definition: A nonhormonal vaginal gel prevents pregnancy when used before intercourse by maintaining acidity, measured as low pH, in the presence of semen and reducing sperm movement.

goal.need: In 2019, 41.6% of US pregnancies were unintended. FDA identifies nonhormonal contraception as an option for women who cannot tolerate hormones or have contraindications to their use, and identifies potential benefit from on-demand dosing for women with infrequent intercourse.

statements.quote: The Panel recommends additional development of female contraceptive modalities that are delivered to the reproductive tract
statements.context: The recommendation concerns blocking egg or sperm function within the female reproductive tract on demand.

statements.quote: we intend to seek regulatory approval for product labeling stating Phexxi can be used on-demand, immediately before or up to one hour before intercourse.
statements.context: The company's annual report for 2019 describes its intended contraceptive indication.

completion.title: FDA approves a vaginal pH-modulating gel for on-demand prevention of pregnancy.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a vaginal pH-modulating gel for prevention of pregnancy in females of reproductive potential as an on-demand method of contraception, with approved dosing and safety labeling. Achieved by Phexxi, NDA 208352, on 22 May 2020. The approved dose is 5 g vaginally immediately before or up to one hour before each act of vaginal intercourse.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, NDA 208352 approval letter and accompanying prescribing information.
completion.threshold_quote: It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.
completion.basis: The approved indication establishes the capability described here. FDA assessed contraceptive efficacy alongside local and urinary safety. The approved label records cystitis, pyelonephritis or other upper urinary infection in 10 of 2,804 exposed participants (0.36%), including one serious case requiring hospitalization.

milestones.title: A vaginal gel keeps a semen mixture below about pH 5 in a laboratory test.
milestones.criterion: Meet the developer's buffering target of pH below about 5 in the presence of semen, using its direct semen-mixing assay and identifying the gel:semen ratio. Example 10 of the developer's patent used semen from five volunteers; Table XII reports pH 4.45 at a 1:2 gel:semen ratio. These patent-reported results are not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: Rush-Presbyterian-St. Luke's Medical Center inventors, formulation target and laboratory assay in US patent 6,706,276, claim 1 and Example 10.
milestones.threshold_quote: wherein the composition maintains an acidic vaginal pH of less than about 5 in the presence of semen ejaculated from the male

milestones.title: FDA permits a 14-day vaginal-gel safety study in women to proceed.
milestones.criterion: FDA reviews the supporting evidence and determines that the 14-day local-tolerance study A02-074 in women can proceed under IND 64623. FDA's regulatory history records this determination after an overseas phase 1 study and nonclinical testing that included a 10-day rabbit vaginal-irritation study.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, regulatory history for IND 64623 reproduced in the NDA 208352 multidisciplinary review.
milestones.threshold_quote: Both study protocols were reviewed and determined to be safe to proceed.

milestones.title: A vaginal gel yields fewer than one forward-moving sperm per microscope field in a postcoital test.
milestones.criterion: A satisfactory ACIDFORM postcoital test has fewer than one progressively motile (forward-moving) sperm per high-power microscope field in midcycle cervical mucus, averaged across the fields examined. The 2004 crossover study in 20 sterilized women reported group means of 0.19 after application 0–30 minutes before intercourse and 0.75 after application 8–10 hours beforehand, versus 17.94 without gel. These group means do not establish that every individual test passed.
milestones.set_by: ACIDFORM postcoital-study investigators; the study-specific cutoff is restated by co-investigator Christine K. Mauck and Kathleen L. Vincent in their 2020 account.
milestones.threshold_quote: the cut-off of less than one PMS/HPF in the later Acidform study

milestones.title: A vaginal gel's seven-cycle pregnancy rate has an upper 95% confidence limit of at most 21%.
milestones.criterion: AMPOWER requires the upper 95% confidence limit of its Kaplan–Meier seven-cycle typical-use pregnancy estimate to be ≤21%, in women aged 18–35 using 5 g before each act of intercourse. Evaluable cycles exclude backup contraception, no intercourse and lengths outside 21–35 days. Among 1,183 women contributing 4,769 evaluable cycles, 101 pregnancies yielded 13.7% (95% CI 10.0–17.5%).
milestones.set_by: Evofem, Inc., AMPOWER protocol AMP002, registered as NCT03243305, version 4 dated 1 November 2017, sections 9.2 and 9.8.
milestones.threshold_quote: the upper limit of the 95% CI of the cumulative seven-cycle pregnancy rate is less than or equal to 21%.

results.finding: CONRAD submitted IND 64,623 for Acidform vaginal contraceptive gel; study sample size not reported.
results.detail: The FDA review also reports a 10-day rabbit vaginal-irritation study. It does not report the A02-074 study, an overseas phase 1 study, or FDA's determination that A02-074 could proceed.
results.quote:
April 29 – Submission of IND 64,623 for Acidform Gel as vaginal contraceptive gel by 
CONRAD.

results.finding: In 20 sterilized women, ACIDFORM yielded a mean of 0.19 progressively motile sperm per high-power field.
results.detail: ACIDFORM was applied 0–30 minutes before intercourse. The group mean does not establish that every individual test met the criterion.
results.quote: ACIDFORM or N-9 product administered 0-30 min precoitus or ACIDFORM given 8-10 h precoitus significantly reduced the mean number of progressively motile sperm compared to control cycles (0.19, 0.07, 0.75 vs. 17.94, respectively, p<.05, Wilcoxon test).

results.finding: PHEXXI trial, 1,183 subjects: seven-cycle pregnancy rate upper 95% confidence limit was 17.5%.
results.detail: The Kaplan–Meier typical-use estimate was 13.7%. Participants were aged 18–35 and used a 5 g dose before intercourse; specified nonevaluable cycles were excluded.
results.quote:
The 7-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate was 13.7% (95% 
CI: 10.0%, 17.5%), excluding cycles with back-up contraception, cycles <21 days or >35 days in 
length and cycles in which no intercourse was reported.

results.finding: FDA approved Phexxi vaginal gel for on-demand contraception under NDA 208352; sample size not stated.
results.detail: The approval letter identifies the indication and refers to enclosed prescribing information and instructions for use. The excerpt does not state the dose or describe the gel’s pH-modulating mechanism.
results.quote:
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective 
on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon 
labeling.
